wireless.heading: Wireless access points
wireless.lead: Current access points for Wi-Fi in offices, warehouses and outdoors. First choose how you want to manage them, then narrow down with the filters.
wireless.selectorHint: Answer a few questions to find the right access point.
list.none: No model matches these choices. Remove a filter and try again.
list.compareFull: You can compare at most 4 models.
filters.title: Filters
filters.poe: How much power (PoE) does my switch give?
filters.poeHint: Models that work fully on the power you pick are shown.
filters.mgig: Fast link (2.5 Gb/s and up, mGig)
filters.featuresHint: Every feature you pick must be on the model.
filters.older: Also show models that are no longer sold
tray.need: Select at least 2 models to compare.
tray.label: Comparison selection
detail.variantsLead: This model is ordered under the codes below. Confirm the code in the Cisco ordering guide.
detail.askLead: Answer a few questions on the Find my model page.
detail.eosTitle: This model is no longer proposed for new projects
detail.eosAnnounced: Cisco has announced the end of sale of this model. Last order date: {date}. Last date of support: {ldos}.
detail.eosReached: This model is no longer sold. The last order date {date} has passed. Last date of support: {ldos}.
selector.title: Find my model (wireless)
selector.lead: Answer five short questions. We suggest up to 3 current access points; models that are no longer sold are never shown.
selector.q.env: 1. Where will the access point go?
selector.q.poe: 3. How much power (PoE) does your switch give over the network cable?
selector.q.density: 4. How many people will connect at once?
selector.q.future: 5. How important is the newest technology?
selector.o.future.sixghz: I want the 6 GHz band (Wi-Fi 6E or 7)
selector.pending: Pick your answers and press "Suggest models".
selector.none: No current model fits these answers. Change an answer and try again.
selector.assumption.1: Only models that are on sale (current) are suggested.
selector.assumption.2: The number of people is judged roughly by the radio and stream count; this is not a Cisco sizing figure.
selector.assumption.3: The power class you pick is compared with the class the model needs for full function.
selector.assumption.4: The licence, the regulatory code added to the ordering code and the real cabling must be confirmed per project.
selector.relaxed.density: No model fits your number of people exactly, so the closest models are shown.
selector.relaxed.poe: No model works fully on the power you picked, so the closest models are shown; see the PoE warnings.
selector.why.recommended: the recommended model of its series
selector.why.mgmt.unified: can be managed on-premises or in the cloud
selector.warn.poe-short: Warning: full function needs {need}; on your switch some features are off or the speed drops.
selector.warn.poe-needed: Note: full function needs {need}. Check that your switch provides it.
selector.warn.six-ghz-turkey: Confirm the 6 GHz status in Türkiye: its use depends on BTK rules.
compare.title: Compare
compare.lead: See 2 to 4 models side by side. Your selection lives in the link in the address bar, so you can share it.
compare.empty: You have not picked any model yet. Tick the "Compare" boxes on a family page.
compare.one: One model is selected. Add at least one more to compare.
compare.noDiff: The models you picked are the same on these rows.
compare.nojs: The comparison table needs JavaScript. You can read each model on its own detail page.
selector.nojs: The suggestion form needs JavaScript. You can browse the models one by one on the wireless page.
val.poetype.poe: PoE (802.3af, up to 15.4 W per port)
val.poetype.poe_plus: PoE+ (802.3at, up to 30 W per port)
switching.heading: Switches
switching.lead: Current switches that connect the computers, phones, cameras and access points of an office or branch. Choose how you want to manage them first, then narrow down by ports, PoE and speed.
switching.selectorHint: Answer a few questions to find the switch that fits your ports and PoE.
routing.heading: Routers and Meraki MX
routing.lead: Current routers and Meraki MX security appliances that connect a branch to the internet and the head office. Choose how you want to manage them first, then narrow down by speed and number of links.
routing.selectorHint: Answer a few questions to find the router that fits your speed and links.
detail.poeNone: This switch does not give PoE; the devices need their own power supply.
detail.poeLead: The total power of the cameras, phones and access points you connect must not exceed this budget.
detail.perfNoSec: The encrypted speed is not verified for this model.
detail.perfNote: The figures are the "up to" values in the datasheets; real speed depends on settings and licence.
detail.replacementNone: Cisco names no replacement for this model.
filters.sw.poeHint: The total PoE power must cover the cameras, phones and access points you connect.
filters.sw.poeAny: No PoE needed / does not matter
filters.rt.thrHint: Routing speed is the highest value in the datasheet; it is lower for encrypted traffic.
filters.rt.secHint: The real speed with VPN or security features on. This speed depends on a licence.
filters.rt.poe: Must be able to give PoE
selector.sw.title: Find my model (switch)
selector.sw.lead: Answer six short questions. We suggest up to 3 current switches; models that are no longer sold are never shown.
selector.sw.nojs: The suggestion form needs JavaScript. You can browse the models one by one on the switch page.
selector.sw.q.ports: 1. How many devices (ports) will you connect?
selector.sw.q.poeCount: 2. How many of them will be powered by PoE (IP phones, cameras, access points)?
selector.sw.q.poeWatts: 3. How much power does a PoE device draw on average?
selector.sw.q.uplink: 5. How fast should the uplink to the core be?
selector.sw.o.poeWatts.30: Medium (camera, Wi-Fi 6 access point, about 30 W)
selector.sw.o.mgmt.on_prem: On-premises (Catalyst Center or my own management)
selector.sw.why.recommended: the recommended model of its series
selector.sw.why.poe: its {p1} W PoE budget covers your need ({p2} W)
selector.sw.why.mgmt.unified: can be managed on-premises or in the cloud
selector.sw.warn.poe-short: Warning: the PoE budget is {p1} W and the estimated need is {p2} W. Some devices may not work on this model.
selector.sw.warn.poe-psu: Note: {p1} W is with the default power supply; a second supply can raise the budget (see the model page).
selector.sw.relaxed.poe: No model gives as much PoE as you need; the models with the biggest PoE budget are shown. See the warnings.
selector.sw.assumption.1: Only models that are on sale (current) are suggested.
selector.sw.assumption.2: The PoE need is the number of PoE devices times the power per device; this is a rule of thumb, the real need depends on the devices.
selector.sw.assumption.3: The PoE budget is the value with the model's default power supply; on some models a second supply raises it.
selector.sw.assumption.4: Licence, power supply and real cabling must be checked for each project.
selector.rt.title: Find my model (routing)
selector.rt.lead: Answer six short questions. We suggest up to 3 current routers or Meraki MX appliances; models that are no longer sold are never shown.
selector.rt.nojs: The suggestion form needs JavaScript. You can browse the models one by one on the routing page.
selector.rt.q.size: 1. How fast is the branch's internet link?
selector.rt.q.wan: 2. How many internet links will there be?
selector.rt.q.cellular: 4. Do you need a cellular (LTE/5G) backup link?
selector.rt.q.where: 6. A physical device or a virtual one in the cloud?
selector.rt.o.where.virtual: Virtual (vMX for AWS, Azure or Google Cloud)
selector.rt.why.recommended: the recommended model of its series
selector.rt.why.mgmt.unified: can be managed on-premises or in the cloud
selector.rt.why.cellular.pluggable: a cellular module can be added
selector.rt.why.virtual: a virtual device that runs in the cloud
selector.rt.warn.thr-short: Warning: the routing speed is {p1} Mb/s and you need {p2} Mb/s.
selector.rt.warn.security: Note: with VPN encryption or advanced security on, the speed is {p1} Mb/s; this speed depends on a licence.
selector.rt.warn.licence: This model needs a licence; see the model page.
selector.rt.relaxed.size: No model is as fast as you need; the fastest models are shown. See the warnings.
selector.rt.assumption.1: Only models that are on sale (current) are suggested.
selector.rt.assumption.2: Speed is the highest routing value in the datasheet; it is lower with VPN and security features on.
selector.rt.assumption.3: Meraki devices need a licence for every device; for Catalyst routers confirm the licence requirement with your partner.
selector.rt.assumption.4: The cellular link (SIM and carrier), modules and real cabling must be checked for each project.
config.title: Configuration: uplink module
config.lead: The uplink of this switch is chosen with a module. The module fits the switch's {n} module slot. Only modules that the Cisco datasheet confirms for this model are listed.
config.note: This is a draft: the order code does not include the licence tier (for example -E or -A), power supplies or cables. For a real order use the Cisco ordering guide or confirm with your partner.
selector.sw.warn.poe-class: Warning: the ports of this model give at most {p1} W and your devices need {p2} W. Those devices will not run at full power.
selector.sw.warn.uplink-module: Note: the uplink speed you asked for comes from a network module that is ordered separately (see the configuration on the model page).
detail.perfLegacy: The speed of this older model is not verified; it is not used in new projects.

search.lead: Type a model name, part number (PID), feature, story title or term. Turkish letters are optional (for example “isik”), and small typos are fine.
search.label: Search for
search.error: The search index could not be loaded. Reload the page and try again.
search.noscript: Search needs JavaScript to be turned on in your browser.
search.hint: Type something; results appear as you type.
search.noneTip: Try only the first part of the part number, or a shorter word.
hero.search.label: Search models, part numbers or terms
glossary.title: Glossary
glossary.lead: Every term explained behind a “?” button on the site. If you meet a technical term or abbreviation, look it up here.
shortlist.title: My shortlist
shortlist.full: The list is full (at most {n} models). Remove one first.
shortlist.saveFailed: The browser does not allow saving; the list only lasts while this page is open.
shortlist.addConfig: Add this configuration to my shortlist
shortlist.lead: Collect the models you like here; print them, download a file that opens in Excel, or share a link. The list is stored only in this browser and needs no account.
shortlist.notQuote: This list contains no prices, stock or quote and is not an order. Have your Cisco partner verify the part numbers before ordering.
shortlist.error: The model information could not be loaded. Reload the page and try again.
shortlist.empty: Your list is empty. Use “Add to my shortlist” on a model page, in the model finder or in a comparison.
shortlist.copied: Link copied. Whoever opens it sees the same list.
shortlist.clearConfirm: Remove every model from the list?
shortlist.configNote: Draft configuration: power supplies, licences and cables are not included.
shortlist.notCurrent: This model is no longer current; choose its replacement for a quote.
shortlist.missing: This model is no longer on the site. You can remove it from the list.
shortlist.shared: This list was opened from a link ({n} models). You are only viewing it.
shortlist.savedShared: The list was added to your shortlist.
migration.lead: Type the name or part number of the old model. We show the current replacement and what changes (management, licence, power, ports).
migration.label: Name or part number of the old model
migration.hint: Type a model; results appear as you type.
migration.error: The old-model list could not be loaded. Reload the page and try again.
migration.none: “{q}” is not in our list of old models.
migration.noneTip: Our list only holds models whose end of sale is announced or reached and confirmed by a Cisco notice. Try only the first part of the part number; the code may be written differently.
migration.noChanges: No difference in the features we compare.
migration.listTitle: Old models you can look up ({n})
migration.listHelp: Tap one and we show the result.
